To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the direct cortical response is a compound potential with a positive and negative component, and that the negative component of the direct cortical reponse can be facilitated by stimulation of the posterior and lateral hypothalamus.
the DCR can be facilitated by stimulation of the posterior region of the hypothalamus.

the negative component of the direct cortical responses (DCRs) undergoes a reversal to positive during “fatigue” (stimulation of the cortex at 10/sec) and that the negative component can be restored during prolonged stimulation of the cervical sympathic nerve (CSN).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the cervical sympathetic nerves and the hypothalamus on the direct cortical response in rats.
the influence of the sympathetic system and hypothalamus upon the direct cortical response, and the possible mechanisms of the effects observed.
the influence of the hypothalamus and cervical sympathetic nerve on the direct cortical response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hypothalamus influences the dendritic and somatic components of the DCR in a similar manner.
the negative DCR is a result of dendritic activity.
the hypothalamus has a facilitatory effect on the negative DCR, while the CSN exerts an inhibitory effect on it, and the latter effect can be reversed by prolonged stimulation of the CSN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the negative component of the DRC is a manifestation of a GABA-mediated inhibitory process.
the hypothalamus influences the DCR in a similar way to the CSN.
the DCRs are a result of the activity of the dendrites of pyramidal cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the negative phase of DCR is a manifestation of the inhibitory processes in the cortex.
the hypothalamus has a facilitatory influence upon DCRs.
the hypothalamus is a powerful facilitator of the negative component of the DSR.
